item.title: How We Finally Conquered Our Tiny Balcony (and Got Our Morning Coffee Back!)
item.description: Alright, fellow tiny-flat-dwellers! Let me paint you a picture you’ll probably recognise. My partner, Liam, and I live in a lovely, if slightly snug, two-bed flat in Bristol. We love it, honestly. Great location, decent rent (for Bristol, anyway), and only a minor battle with the neighbour over bin collection day. But for years, there was one corner of our little home that brought us nothing but profound sadness: the balcony.

item.title: How We Transformed a Poky Victorian Kitchenette into a Proper Working Space
item.description:
You know the feeling. You move into what the estate agent optimistically calls a “compact Victorian terrace” in a nice part of North London, and when you actually see the kitchen, you realise it was built when people ate bread and margarine for dinner and never, ever cooked. The kitchen in our flat was 1.8 metres wide. I measured it twice. I’m not proud of that.

Three months later, having spent roughly £1,800 and an embarrassing amount of time on Pinterest, we’ve actually got a kitchen you can stand in without your hips brushing both walls simultaneously. More importantly, we can now cook an actual meal without feeling like we’re in a test of human endurance.

item.title: Flexible Furniture That Doesn't Look Temporary
item.description:
When you’re renting in the UK, you learn pretty quickly that furniture is a pain.

You can’t drill into walls for proper shelves (or at least, you’re not supposed to). You can’t swap out the landlord’s terrible built-in wardrobe. And you definitely don’t want to buy a massive three-seater sofa that you’ll have to drag up three flights of stairs when you inevitably move flats next year.

I’ve been renting for about six years now, and I’ve gone through a fair few “furniture phases.” The bulky phase, where I bought stuff that looked nice but was a nightmare to move. The cheap IKEA phase, where everything fell apart after one flat move. And finally, the flexible phase – where I only buy stuff that adapts, folds, or packs down.
